newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Astra says new Kijang van orders up.
newsitem.headline: Astra says new Kijang van orders up.

text.p: Indonesia's largest car maker PT Astra International said on Tuesday it had received orders for up to 9,600 units of its newly-launched Kijang model.
"We have received orders for up to 9,600 units until last night. It (sales) is much better than expected," Astra finance director Rini Suwandi told reporters.
She said Astra had so far delivered 3,000 new Kijang vans, launched this month, and expected to deliver at least 5,000 units per month beginning in March.
Suwandi said the Timor sedans produced by a company controlled by President Suharto's youngest son, Hutomo Mandala Putra, appeared to have little impact on Kijang sales.
"Most Indonesians like vans which can carry between eight to nine passengers, rather than sedans." she said.
Suwandi said car sales were likely to recover this year with total sales of cars in the domestic market to be at the same level as in 1995.
She said car sales fell slightly in 1996 because of the Timor car issue. She did not give further details.
